title: Estimating a population by quadrat sampling
goal: See how the population density of a plant species is found from the plants counted in quadrats.
note: Quadrats are placed at random in a field and the plants of one species are counted in each. The population density is the total count divided by the total area of the quadrats.

controls.label: Total plants counted in all the quadrats

graphs.title: The population density rises in a straight line as more plants are counted.
graphs.label: Population density

sentences: Ten quadrats, each one square metre, are placed at random in the school field.
The density is the total number of plants counted divided by the total area of all the quadrats.

predict.prompt: The same quadrats are used in two fields, and more plants are counted in the first field. Which field has the higher population density?
predict.reveal: Raise the number of plants counted and watch the population density.

concept_check.question: How is the population density of a species estimated by quadrat sampling?
options: The total number of individuals divided by the total area of the quadrats
The number of quadrats divided by the number of individuals
The area of the field divided by the number of quadrats
concept_check.explanation: Density is the average number of individuals per unit area, so the count in all the quadrats is divided by the total area of those quadrats.

hints: A quadrat is a small sample of the whole field.
Which two things decide the total area that was sampled?
Divide the total count by the total area sampled.
